title: Three random decks
notes: Keep one adult at each table. Every band opens with a short game (P1); it gives the decks a question but cannot show the cycle, which comes from counting pairs. For K-1 Problems 2-4, split the pictured pairs among the children and pool a complete shared nine-pair page for each comparison. Then bring the three comparisons together to check the cycle; each child need not make 27 records. On return, K-1 can play the advantage game (P5), change one card or swap (P6-7), then try P8-9 if ready. Grades 2-3 share and pool comparisons for P2 and new arrangements in P4; P3 is a hidden-bag guessing game without another exhaustive tally. On return they can choose altered decks, duplication or exact totals (P4-7). Grades 4-5 can replay P1 after counting P2, then choose one complete search, duplication comparison or two-card obstruction (P3-8) as its own visit.
